items.name: Wicker Basket
items.desc: The sturdy wicker basket that came with the laundry room and has caught more socks than anyone has counted.

items.name: Plastic Hamper
items.desc: A lightweight hamper with slots in the sides, in a shade of blue that only exists for hampers.

items.name: Wire Basket
items.desc: A chrome wire basket from the closet of a very organized person.

items.name: Drawstring Laundry Bag
items.desc: A soft laundry bag with a wide, forgiving mouth that swallows shots that were only nearly good.

items.name: Tiny Doll Basket
items.desc: A wicker basket sized for a doll's laundry, which turns every shot into a small act of faith.

items.name: Pool Floatie
items.desc: A striped pool ring with a net slung underneath that still smells faintly of summer.

items.name: Hollow Log
items.desc: A mossy hollow log that has clearly been home to at least one family of chipmunks.

items.name: Claw Machine Bin
items.desc: The prize chute from an arcade claw machine, finally catching something.

items.name: Spring Ribbon Basket
items.desc: A wicker basket tied with a ribbon, clearly meant for something more festive than socks.

items.name: Beach Tote
items.desc: A canvas beach tote with a little sand in the bottom that will never fully leave.

items.name: Apple Bushel Basket
items.desc: A bushel basket that once held apples and still smells faintly of them.

items.name: Frosted Wire Basket
items.desc: A wire basket that looks as if it spent the night on the porch and enjoyed it.

items.name: Standard Dryer
items.desc: The mint green dryer that came with the place; it hums, it tumbles and it asks for nothing.

items.name: Avocado Slow Tumble
items.desc: An avocado green dryer from a better decade that tumbles slowly and means it.

items.name: Laundromat Industrial
items.desc: A steel laundromat dryer that takes bigger Loads and has seen a great many socks.

items.name: Backyard Clothesline
items.desc: Socks come down off the line one at a time, the way laundry used to come in from the yard.

items.name: Portal Dryer
items.desc: A dryer that hums in a key nobody has heard before. It goes on sale when the Odd Bin reaches page 7, and brings portal Loads from page 8.

items.name: Oatmeal Rug
items.desc: A plain oatmeal rug that goes with everything and complains about nothing.

items.name: Braided Oval Rug
items.desc: A braided rug that has been walked on by three generations and several dogs.

items.name: Rag Rug
items.desc: A rug woven from old shirts, one of which you are fairly sure was yours.

items.name: Moss Rug
items.desc: A soft green rug that feels like standing on a lawn that has been asked to behave.

items.name: Sunny Stripe Rug
items.desc: A yellow striped rug that makes the room look sunny on even the grayest wash day.

items.name: Faded Rose Rug
items.desc: A rose colored rug that was bright once and has become something better.

items.name: Checkerboard Linoleum Rug
items.desc: A rug printed to look like the floor it is lying on.

items.name: Old Red Medallion
items.desc: A proper rug that has ended up in a laundry room and is coping.

items.name: Granny Square
items.desc: Crocheted in squares by somebody who watched a lot of television.

items.name: Library Runner
items.desc: Long, narrow and quiet. It has been walked on by serious people.

items.name: Picnic Blanket
items.desc: Red check, one grass stain, and it has never once been to a park.

items.name: Wavy Motel Carpet
items.desc: A pattern chosen to hide absolutely anything, and it does.

items.name: Olive Stripe Kilim
items.desc: Flat woven in olive and cream, with a fringe somebody trimmed.

items.name: Moon Phase Runner
items.desc: The moon, eight times, on a narrow strip of very dark wool.

items.name: Big Daisy
items.desc: One enormous daisy. There is no second daisy and there does not need to be.

items.name: Care Label Rug
items.desc: Woven with washing symbols nobody has ever fully understood.

items.name: Cloud Blue Shag
items.desc: Deep enough to lose a sock in, which has happened.

items.name: Cream Rug With One Scribble
items.desc: Cream, everywhere, except for the one part that is not.

items.name: Woods Window
items.desc: The window looks out on pines and soft hills, with no neighbors in sight.

items.name: City Window
items.desc: The window looks out on rooftops and lit windows, each one with its own laundry going.

items.name: Rainy Window
items.desc: The window looks out on a gray, steady rain that you are not out in.

items.name: Snowy Window
items.desc: The window looks out on snowy pines, which makes warm laundry feel even warmer.

items.name: Freight Train Window
items.desc: A freight train goes past every so often. Nobody has ever counted the cars.

items.name: Neighbor's Laundry Line
items.desc: Their washing is out too. Yours is better and you know it.

items.name: October Rain
items.desc: Bare branches, wet light, and rain running down the glass.

items.name: Pink Dawn
items.desc: The sky doing the one good thing it does before six in the morning.

items.name: Firefly Yard
items.desc: A hedge at dusk with the lights coming on in it.

items.name: Porch Light at Night
items.desc: Somebody left their porch light on. Two moths are dealing with it.

items.name: Found Sock Frame
items.desc: A plain cream frame for an ordinary sock from your Drawer, because ordinary socks matter too.

items.name: Cork Board Frame
items.desc: A cork frame that pins up a sock from your Drawer like a note you want to remember.

items.name: Oak Hero Frame
items.desc: An oak frame that shows off one of the hero socks in your Drawer.

items.name: Brass Hero Frame
items.desc: A little brass frame for a hero sock that deserves a spot on the wall.

items.name: Painted Hero Frame
items.desc: A frame painted robin's egg blue for a hero sock with a lot of personality.

items.name: Gilt Hero Frame
items.desc: A fancy gilt frame for your most distinguished hero sock, whoever that turns out to be.

items.name: Little Succulent
items.desc: A small succulent that asks for sun, a little water and to be left alone.

items.name: Tiny Cactus
items.desc: A tiny cactus in a pink pot, prickly but well meaning.

items.name: Basil Pot
items.desc: A pot of basil that makes the laundry room smell faintly like dinner.

items.name: Spider Plant
items.desc: A spider plant that keeps making babies, which you keep giving to the neighbors.

items.name: Snake Plant
items.desc: A snake plant that has survived everything, including the month you forgot it existed.

items.name: Trailing Pothos
items.desc: A pothos that has quietly claimed the top of the dryer as its own.

items.name: Floor Fern
items.desc: A big fern that thrives on dryer steam and mild neglect.

items.name: Monstera
items.desc: A leafy monstera whose leaves have more holes than your oldest sock.

items.name: Rubber Plant
items.desc: Big glossy leaves that get dusted about once a year.

items.name: Peace Lily
items.desc: Dramatic about water. Recovers instantly and says nothing.

items.name: Stubborn Aloe
items.desc: Has survived four moves and one genuinely bad winter.

items.name: Trailing Ivy
items.desc: It is heading for the clothesline and nobody is stopping it.

items.name: Dried Flowers
items.desc: They were beautiful in June and they are still here in a jar.

items.name: Blob Lamp
items.desc: A glass lamp full of slow orange blobs that make thoughtful shapes while you fold.

items.name: Sea Glass Blob Lamp
items.desc: A blob lamp in sea glass blue, for Loads that would rather be a beach day.

items.name: Grape Soda Blob Lamp
items.desc: A purple blob lamp the exact color of a grape soda from the back of a gas station cooler.

items.name: Swamp Blob Lamp
items.desc: A green blob lamp that bubbles along like a very calm swamp.

items.name: Mushroom Lamp
items.desc: A glass mushroom that glows the colour of weak tea.

items.name: Cherry Cola Lamp
items.desc: Dark red glass with slow bubbles that never quite reach the top.

items.name: Mossy Glass Lamp
items.desc: Green glass that makes the whole corner look like a pond.

items.name: Milk Glass Lamp
items.desc: Plain white glass. It does one job and it does not talk about it.

items.name: Dusk Purple Lamp
items.desc: The exact purple the sky is for about four minutes.

items.name: Laundry Wall Calendar
items.desc: A wall calendar that marks every day you played the Daily Load with a small, proud circle.

items.name: Pine Display Shelf
items.desc: A pine shelf that shows off your rarest hero socks, rolled up and resting.

items.name: Walnut Display Shelf
items.desc: A second shelf for rare socks, because the first one filled up faster than anyone expected.

items.name: Mint Display Shelf
items.desc: A mint painted shelf for the rare socks that like to be seen.

items.name: Chipped Blue Mug
items.desc: A blue mug with a chip on the rim that you always turn to face the wall.

items.name: Mint Green Mug
items.desc: A mint green mug that matches the dryer exactly, which you insist was not planned.

items.name: Tomato Red Mug
items.desc: A cheerful red mug that holds exactly one cup of tea and one good idea.

items.name: Speckled Clay Mug
items.desc: A heavy speckled mug from a pottery class you still bring up at parties.

items.name: Mustard Diner Mug
items.desc: A thick diner mug that makes any coffee taste like a Saturday morning.

items.name: Night Owl Mug
items.desc: A dark mug for Loads folded after the rest of the house has gone to sleep.

items.name: The Tuesday Mug
items.desc: A mug that says Tuesday on it, which is correct about one day a week.

items.name: Corn Festival Mug
items.desc: A souvenir mug from the Corn Festival, where you did not run the 5K but did eat the butter.

items.name: Lake Hoyt Regatta Mug
items.desc: A regatta mug with a tiny sailboat on it that has sailed through the dishwasher for years.

items.name: Grandma's Rose Mug
items.desc: A thin china mug with roses on it that you may use as long as you are careful.

items.name: Worlds Okayest Mug
items.desc: A gift that was funny once and is now simply true.

items.name: Thrift Store Mug
items.desc: Somebody elses initial on it. You have grown into the letter.

items.name: Enamel Camp Mug
items.desc: Chipped down to the metal in three places, all of them the same place.

items.name: Souvenir From Somewhere
items.desc: The place name has worn off. The mug remains loyal.

items.name: The Two Handled One
items.desc: Nobody knows why it has two. It has always had two.

items.name: Paper Star Garland
items.desc: Folded paper stars strung together during one very long phone call.

items.name: Pom Pom Garland
items.desc: A string of yarn pom poms made from the scraps of other projects.

items.name: Felt Ball Garland
items.desc: A string of felt balls that look a lot like tiny sock balls, which is not a coincidence.

items.name: Autumn Leaf Garland
items.desc: Felt leaves in orange and red that stay up long after the real ones have come down.

items.name: Snowflake Garland
items.desc: Paper snowflakes on a string, each one cut slightly wrong and each one perfect.

items.name: Warm String Lights
items.desc: A strand of warm little bulbs that makes the laundry room feel like it is in on something nice.

items.name: Mint Kitchen Clock
items.desc: A mint green clock that ticks just loudly enough to be company.

items.name: Schoolhouse Clock
items.desc: A wooden wall clock that makes every afternoon feel like the last period before the weekend.

items.name: Sunburst Clock
items.desc: A gold sunburst clock that has come back into fashion three separate times.

items.name: Dryer Dial Clock
items.desc: A clock made from an old dryer dial that still clicks a little when the hour turns over.

items.name: Damp Towel Live
items.desc: A tour poster for Damp Towel, a band you have definitely heard of by now.

items.name: Visit Lake Hoyt
items.desc: A faded travel poster promising sailboats, fudge and a very reasonable parking lot.

items.name: Camp Wappalusk
items.desc: A camp poster with a canoe on it and at least four spelling mistakes in the lake song.

items.name: Vote Bartleby
items.desc: A campaign poster for Bartleby, who ran on a platform of fewer puddles.

items.name: Corn Festival 5K
items.desc: A poster for the Corn Festival, which has a 5K, a parade and a surprising amount of butter.

items.name: You Are Doing Fine
items.desc: A motivational poster of a single sock on a mountaintop, looking out at nothing in particular.

items.name: The Great Sock Migration
items.desc: A nature documentary poster about the long journey from the hamper to under the bed.

items.name: Grand Lint Expo
items.desc: An advertisement for the annual Grand Lint Expo, where admission costs one pocketful.

items.name: Moth Appreciation Society
items.desc: A recruitment poster for a society that meets at dusk near the porch light.

items.name: Fold Night at the Grange
items.desc: A flyer for a community folding night; bring your own basket and a covered dish.

items.name: Sock Puppet Hamlet
items.desc: A theater poster for a sock puppet Hamlet that ran for one weekend and made everyone cry.

items.name: The Dryer Has a Back
items.desc: A grainy poster covered in arrows, made by someone with a theory and a lot of red string.

items.name: Slow Tumble Records
items.desc: A poster for a record label whose every album is exactly one dryer cycle long.

items.name: Open 24 Hours
items.desc: A laundromat sign from a laundromat that closed years ago.

items.name: Seed Catalogue Page
items.desc: One page of tomatoes, framed, because the picture was good.

items.name: Tide Chart
items.desc: A tide chart for a coast that is nowhere near here.

items.name: County Fair
items.desc: A fair from a year printed too small to read.

items.name: How To Tie Knots
items.desc: Twelve knots. You have used one of them, once.

items.name: Laundry Cat
items.desc: A cat that sleeps on warm laundry and has never once helped fold it.

items.name: Sage Sprig Paper
items.desc: The paper that was already on the walls when you moved in, and it grows on you.

items.name: Ticking Stripe
items.desc: Narrow stripes that make the ceiling feel further away than it is.

items.name: Pin Dot Paper
items.desc: Small dots in even rows. Nothing about it has ever been in a hurry.

items.name: Kitchen Check
items.desc: A check so mild it could be a tea towel, and probably once was.

items.name: Big Calm Florals
items.desc: Large flowers in even rows. Somebody chose these on purpose.

items.name: Plain Warm White
items.desc: No pattern at all. The socks are the pattern.

items.name: Old Plank Floor
items.desc: The boards that came with the room, worn pale where the table stands.

items.name: Checkerboard Lino
items.desc: Black and cream squares, curling very slightly at one corner.

items.name: Cool Grey Tile
items.desc: Big square tiles that are always four degrees colder than the room.

items.name: Low Pile Carpet
items.desc: Flat brown carpet. Every sock that lands on it is a little harder to find.

items.name: Cork Tiles
items.desc: Pale cork tiles, warm underfoot and quiet, which is most of what a floor is for.

items.name: Painted Grey Boards
items.desc: Boards somebody painted grey one summer and never went back to.

items.name: Apricot Stripe
items.desc: The curtains that were already hanging there, and they still catch the light.

items.name: Blue Gingham
items.desc: Gingham in a small check, hemmed by hand and slightly crooked.

items.name: Small Floral
items.desc: Little flowers on cream. They have been washed more times than the socks.

items.name: Heavy Cream Linen
items.desc: Plain and thick, and they keep the afternoon out when you want them to.

items.name: Lace Panels
items.desc: Lace that turns the window into a lot of very small windows.

items.name: Green Ticking
items.desc: Narrow green lines on ivory. Somebody made these from a mattress cover.

items.name: Green Quilted Mat
items.desc: The mat the table came with, quilted in diamonds and softer every year.

items.name: Flat Oatmeal Mat
items.desc: No texture at all, so every stripe on every sock reads first time.

items.name: Red Gingham Cloth
items.desc: A picnic cloth on a folding table in a laundry room. It works.

items.name: Grey Linen
items.desc: Woven grey that makes a pale sock look like a pale sock and not a ghost.

items.name: Navy Felt
items.desc: Deep blue felt. Everything on it looks a little bit expensive.

items.name: Striped Towel
items.desc: A big towel folded flat, with the soft bands running across it.

items.name: Lofi Beats
items.desc: Soft, dusty beats that loop quietly while you fold.

items.name: Steady Rain
items.desc: Rain on the roof, and nowhere you need to be.

items.name: Vinyl Jazz
items.desc: A brushed snare and a warm crackle from a record nobody remembers buying.

items.name: Someone's TV in the Next Room
items.desc: A game show murmurs through the wall, and it sounds like somebody is winning.

items.name: 90s Hold Music
items.desc: Your call is very important to us, and so is this saxophone solo.

items.name: RESONARC Station
items.desc: A station that composes itself as it plays, so no two Loads sound quite alike.

items.name: Tight Roll
items.desc: Toe to cuff and rolled snug, the way the instructions would say if socks came with instructions.

items.name: Loose Lump
items.desc: Two socks, loosely acquainted, bundled with more hope than technique.

items.name: Tucked
items.desc: One cuff folded back over the whole bundle, as neat as an envelope.

items.name: The Way Your Mom Did It
items.desc: Folded, rolled and tucked with a precision you have never quite managed to copy.

items.name: Lint Sparkle
items.desc: Every shot leaves a glittering drift of lint, which is the only time lint has ever been glamorous.

items.name: Dust Puff
items.desc: Every shot trails a soft puff of dust, as if the ball just came out from under the bed.

items.name: Tiny Hearts
items.desc: Every shot leaves a little trail of hearts, because the pair is simply happy to be together.

items.name: Uncle Energy
items.desc: Socks with firm opinions about the grill start turning up in your Loads, though you still have to find them.

items.name: Gas Station
items.desc: Loud little prints from the spinning rack by the register start turning up in your Loads.

items.name: Fake Merch
items.desc: Free socks from events you may or may not have attended start turning up in your Loads.

items.name: Cursed
items.desc: Socks that are a little bit wrong, and perfectly nice about it, start turning up in your Loads.

items.name: Page 1: Oh. Hi.
items.desc: An odd sock clears its throat and introduces the Odd Bin.

items.name: Page 2: Where We Went
items.desc: The Bin compares notes on where everyone went, and nobody agrees.

items.name: Page 3: The Back
items.desc: A toe sock counts to five and arrives at a theory about the dryer.

items.name: Odd Eye Lamp
items.desc: A small lamp with two mismatched shades, given to you by the Odd Bin as a thank you.

items.name: Page 4: It's Fine
items.desc: The tube sock who has waited the longest would like you to know that it is fine.

items.name: Somehow Still Clean
items.desc: It has been through every Load for years and has never once needed a wash.

items.name: Page 5: A Different House
items.desc: A sock comes back smelling like somebody else's house.

items.name: Page 6: The Vote
items.desc: Half the Bin wants to go looking, and the other half wants to wait.

items.name: Page 7: Someone Went
items.desc: Someone climbs into the back of the dryer and nothing comes back, and after this page the Portal Dryer goes on sale.

items.name: Page 8: The Polite Ones
items.desc: The first portal Load brings socks that belong to no one, and they are extremely polite about it.

items.name: Glowing Lint
items.desc: A pinch of lint from the back of the dryer that glows a soft blue and hums along with the dryer.

items.name: Page 9: They Can Stay
items.desc: The Bin holds a very short meeting and decides the strangers can stay.

items.name: The Sock With No Inside
items.desc: You can turn it inside out all afternoon, and it will politely stay exactly the same.

items.name: Postcard From the Back
items.desc: A postcard from the back of the dryer, addressed to nobody and signed by everyone.

items.name: Page 10: Two Lines
items.desc: The tube sock's mate arrives at last, and the page is only two lines long.

items.name: Tiny Welcome Mat
items.desc: A tiny mat the Odd Bin wove out of lint so the socks from the back of the dryer would feel at home.

items.name: Page 11: The Map
items.desc: A sock draws a map of the back of the dryer in lint, and it is wrong in eleven places and loved anyway.

items.name: Page 12: The Whole Thing
items.desc: Everyone in the Bin has something to say to you, and it is short.

items.name: Knitted From a Clear Night
items.desc: Look long enough and its brightest stars make the shape of a sock, which it insists is a coincidence.

items.name: Something for the Wall
items.desc: A frame the whole Odd Bin made for you out of lint, patience and one borrowed shoelace.
